title: Temurah 14
description: Chapter 2, Yesh BaKorbanot, opens with how offerings of an individual differ from communal offerings, and the Gemara turns to missed libations by night and by day, Rav Dimi’s letter and the ban on writing down halakhot, the verse “These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed seasons,” and why Absalom went to Hebron.
topics: 🐑 Individual and communal offerings: substitution, males and females, compensation, Shabbat and impurity
⏰ Rabbi Meir: any offering whose time is fixed overrides Shabbat and impurity
🍷 Missed libations: “each day on its own day,” “their meal offerings and their libations,” and “beside the Shabbatot of the Lord”
🌙 Are libations sacrificed at night? Rami bar Ḥama, Rava, Rav Yosef and Rav Dimi
✉️ Rav Dimi’s letter: “Those who write halakhot are like those who burn the Torah”
📜 “It is time to work for the Lord”: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish read a scroll of aggada
🗓️ “These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed seasons”: what may be brought on the intermediate days
👑 Absalom’s vow in Hebron, and forty years from when?

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר, וְיֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד, שֶׁקׇּרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה.

a2.he: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד נוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בִּזְכָרִים בֵּין בִּנְקֵבוֹת, וְקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר אֵין נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּזְכָרִים. קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן וּבְאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶם, וְקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר אֵין חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן וְלֹא בְּאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶן, אֲבָל חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶן מִשֶּׁקָּרַב הַזֶּבַח.

a3.he: יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר מַה שֶּׁאֵין בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד, שֶׁקׇּרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶת הַטּוּמְאָה, וְקׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד אֵינָן דּוֹחוֹת לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה.

a4.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: וַהֲלֹא חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וּפַר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד הֵן, וְדוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶת הַטּוּמְאָה! אֶלָּא שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ.

a5.he: גְּמָ׳ קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה כּוּ׳. וּכְלָלָא הוּא? וַהֲרֵי עוֹפוֹת דְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, וְאֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה! כִּי קָתָנֵי — בִּבְהֵמָה קָתָנֵי.

a6.he: וַהֲרֵי וָלָד דְּקָרְבַּן יָחִיד הוּא, וְאֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה! הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

a7.he: וַהֲרֵי תְּמוּרָה עַצְמָהּ, דְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד הִיא, וְאֵין תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה! כִּי קָתָנֵי — בְּעִיקַּר זִיבְחָא קָתָנֵי.

a8.he: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, בְּעִיקַּר זִיבְחָא קָתָנֵי.

a9.he: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד נוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בִּזְכָרִים בֵּין בִּנְקֵבוֹת. וּכְלָלָא הוּא? וַהֲרֵי עוֹלָה, דְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, וְזָכָר אָתְיָא, נְקֵבָה לָא אָתְיָא!

a10.he: הָאִיכָּא עוֹלַת הָעוֹף, דְּתַנְיָא: תַּמּוּת וְזַכְרוּת בִּבְהֵמָה, וְאֵין תַּמּוּת וְזַכְרוּת בָּעוֹפוֹת.

a11.he: וַהֲרֵי חַטָּאת, דְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד הִיא, וּנְקֵבָה אָתְיָא, זָכָר לָא אָתְיָא? הַאִיכָּא שְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא, דְּמַיְיתֵי זָכָר.

a12.he: וְהָאִיכָּא אֲשַׁם יָחִיד, דְּזָכָר אָתֵי, נְקֵבָה לָא אָתֵי? כִּי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן קׇרְבָּן דְּשָׁוֵי בֵּין בְּיָחִיד בֵּין בְּצִיבּוּר — אָשָׁם בְּיָחִיד אִיתֵיהּ, בְּצִבּוּר לֵיתֵיהּ. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִי קָתָנֵי ״כׇּל קׇרְבְּנוֹת״? ״יֵשׁ בְּקׇרְבְּנוֹת״ קָתָנֵי, וּמַאי נִיהוּ — שְׁלָמִים, וְאִי בָּעֵי נְקֵבָה מַיְיתֵי, וְאִי בָּעֵי זָכָר מַיְיתֵי.

a13.he: קׇרְבְּנוֹת יָחִיד חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן [כּוּ׳]. מְנָא לַן?

a14.he: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״דְּבַר יוֹם״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל הַיּוֹם כָּשֵׁר לְמוּסָפִין, ״בְּיוֹמוֹ״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִם עָבַר הַיּוֹם וְלֹא הֱבִיאָן אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן.

a15.he: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּת נִסְכֵּיהֶם, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּרַב הַזֶּבַח? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״ בַּלַּיְלָה, ״מִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״ לְמָחָר.

a16.he: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״מִלְּבַד שַׁבָּתוֹת ה׳״.

a17.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מִלְּבַד שַׁבְּתוֹת ה׳״ — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: בַּיּוֹם — אִין, וּבַלַּיְלָה — לָא. אָמַר קְרָא ״וּמִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״. וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״ וְלָא כְּתַב ״מִלְּבַד שַׁבְּתוֹת ה׳״ — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: (בלילה) [בְּלֵילְיָה] — אִין, בִּימָמָא — לָא.

a18.he: וּמַאי שְׁנָא? מִשּׁוּם דִּבְקָדָשִׁים לַיְלָה הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַיּוֹם, צְרִיכִי.

a19.he: וּנְסָכִים מִי קָרְבִי בַּלַּיְלָה? וְהָתְנַן: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִיקְרַב בַּלַּיְלָה, כְּגוֹן אֵבָרִים וּפְדָרִים, שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין מִבּוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וּמִתְעַכְּלִין וְהוֹלְכִין כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה כּוּלּוֹ.

a20.he: דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִיקְרַב בַּיּוֹם, כְּגוֹן הַקּוֹמֶץ, הַלְּבוֹנָה, וּמִנְחַת נְסָכִים, שֶׁמַּעֲלָן מִבּוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ. מִבּוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ?! וְהָאָמְרַתְּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִיקְרַב בַּיּוֹם נִינְהוּ! אֶלָּא עִם בֹּא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, שֶׁמִּתְעַכְּלִין וְהוֹלְכִין כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעֹלָה״ — רִיבָּה.

a21.he: קָתָנֵי מִיהָא נְסָכִים בַּיּוֹם! אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן לִיקְדַּשׁ, כָּאן לִיקְרַב.

a22.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי מִיקְדָּשׁ קָדְשִׁי קָרוֹבֵי מִיקָּרְבִי, וְהָא תַּנְיָא: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַקָּרֵב בַּיּוֹם — אֵין קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם, וְכׇל הַקָּרֵב בַּלַּיְלָה — קָדוֹשׁ בַּלַּיְלָה, בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בְּלַיְלָה — קָדוֹשׁ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה! אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: סְמִי ״מִנְחַת נְסָכִים״ מֵהָא מַתְנִיתָא.

a23.he: כִּי סְלֵיק רַב דִּימִי, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב יִרְמְיָה דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִנַּיִן לִנְסָכִים הַבָּאִים עִם הַזֶּבַח שֶׁאֵין קְרֵיבִין אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וּלְנִסְכֵּיכֶם וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם״ — מָה שְׁלָמִים בַּיּוֹם, אַף נְסָכִים בַּיּוֹם.

a24.he: אָמַר: אִי אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ דְּכָתֵיב אִיגַּרְתָּא, שְׁלַחִי לֵיהּ לְרַב יוֹסֵף,

b1.he: וְלָא תִּיסְמֵי ״מִנְחַת נְסָכִים״ מִמַּתְנִיתָא. וְלָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן בִּנְסָכִים הַבָּאִין עִם הַזֶּבַח, כָּאן בִּנְסָכִים הַבָּאִין בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן.

b2.he: וְאִי הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִיגַּרְתָּא, מִי אֶפְשָׁר לְמִישְׁלְחַהּ? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כּוֹתְבֵי הֲלָכוֹת (כְּשׂוֹרֵף) [כְּשׂוֹרְפֵי] תוֹרָה, וְהַלָּמֵד מֵהֶן אֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל שָׂכָר.

b3.he: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״כְּתׇב לְךָ אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה״, וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״כִּי עַל פִּי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה״ — לוֹמַר לָךְ: דְּבָרִים שֶׁעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן בִּכְתָב, וְשֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן עַל פֶּה.

b4.he: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״כְּתׇב לְךָ אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה״ — אֵלֶּה אַתָּה כּוֹתֵב, אֲבָל אֵין אַתָּה כּוֹתֵב הֲלָכוֹת!

b5.he: אָמְרִי: דִּלְמָא מִילְּתָא חַדְתָּא שָׁאנֵי, דְּהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מְעַיְּינִי בְּסִיפְרָא דְּאַגַּדְתָּא בְּשַׁבְּתָא, וְדָרְשִׁי הָכִי: ״עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ״, אָמְרִי: מוּטָב תֵּיעָקֵר תּוֹרָה, וְאַל תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.

b6.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ נְסָכִים הַבָּאִין בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן קְרֵיבִין אֲפִילּוּ בַּלַּיְלָה, נִזְדַּמְּנוּ נְסָכִים בַּלַּיְלָה — מַקְדִּישִׁין בַּלַּיְלָה וּמַקְרִיבִין.

b7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּיע לָךְ, ״זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַקָּרֵב בַּיּוֹם — אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם, וְכׇל הַקָּרֵב בַּלַּיְלָה — קָדוֹשׁ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה״.

b8.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וַעֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר פּוֹסֶלֶת בָּהֶן, כְּאֵבָרִין.

b9.he: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: ״אֵלֶּה תַּעֲשׂוּ לַה׳ בְּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם״ — אֵלּוּ חוֹבוֹת הַבָּאוֹת חוֹבָה בָּרֶגֶל.

b10.he: ״לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבוֹתֵיכֶם״ — לִימֵּד עַל נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת שֶׁקְּרֵבִין בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.

b11.he: ״וּלְעוֹלוֹתֵיכֶם״ — בְּמָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר? אִי בְּעוֹלַת נֶדֶר — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר ״נִדְרֵיכֶם״, וְאִי בְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר ״וְנִדְבוֹתֵיכֶם״! הָא אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּעוֹלַת יוֹלֶדֶת וְעוֹלַת מְצוֹרָע.

b12.he: ״וּלְמִנְחוֹתֵיכֶם״ — בְּמָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר? אִי בְּמִנְחַת נֶדֶר — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר, אִי בְּמִנְחַת נְדָבָה — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר! הָא אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּמִנְחַת סוֹטָה וּבְמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת.

b13.he: ״וּלְנִסְכֵּיכֶם וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם״ — מַקִּישׁ נְסָכִים לִשְׁלָמִים: מָה שְׁלָמִים בַּיּוֹם, אַף נְסָכִים בַּיּוֹם. ״וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם״ — לְרַבּוֹת שַׁלְמֵי נָזִיר.

b14.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְלֵימָא מָר שַׁלְמֵי פֶסַח, דְּאִי שַׁלְמֵי נָזִיר — נִידָּר וְנִידָּב הוּא.

b15.he: דְּהָתַנְיָא זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא נִידָּב וְנִידָּר — קָרֵב בְּבָמַת יָחִיד, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִידָּב וְנִידָּר — אֵינוֹ קָרֵב בְּבָמַת יָחִיד.

b16.he: וּתְנַן: הַמְּנָחוֹת וְהַנְּזִירוֹת קְרֵיבִין בְּבָמַת יָחִיד, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר! סְמִי מִכָּאן ״נְזִירוֹת״.

b17.he: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּנָזִיר לָאו נִידָּר וְנִידָּב הוּא? וְהָכְתִיב: ״מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵלְכָה נָּא וַאֲשַׁלֵּם אֶת נִדְרִי אֲשֶׁר נָדַרְתִּי לַה׳ בְּחֶבְרוֹן כִּי נֵדֶר נָדַר עַבְדְּךָ וְגוֹ׳״, מַאי לָאו אַקׇּרְבָּן?

b18.he: לָא, אַעִיקַּר נִדְרוֹ אָמְרִי. עִיקַּר נִדְרוֹ בְּחֶבְרוֹן הֲוָה? וַהֲלֹא בִּגְשׁוּר הֲוָה!

b19.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן: לֹא הָלַךְ אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶלָּא לְהָבִיא כְּבָשִׂים מֵחֶבְרוֹן. הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי תֵּימָא לְאַקְרוֹבֵי הוּא דְּאָזֵיל — שָׁבֵיק יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְאָזֵיל וּמַקְרֵיב בְּחֶבְרוֹן?

b20.he: וְאֶלָּא מַאי? לְהָבִיא כְּבָשִׂים מֵחֶבְרוֹן? הַאי ״אֲשֶׁר נָדַרְתִּי לַה׳ בְּחֶבְרוֹן״, ״מֵחֶבְרוֹן״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!

b21.he: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם לְאַקְרוֹבֵי, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ: אַמַּאי שָׁבֵק יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וּמַקְרֵיב בְּחֶבְרוֹן? תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ גִּבְעוֹן, דְּמָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ הוּא! אֶלָּא, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּתְּרוּ הַבָּמוֹת — כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּבָעֵי מַקְרֵיב.

b22.he: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, לְמַאן? תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: ״מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה״ שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ, דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ, אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה עֲשִׂירִית שֶׁל שְׁמוּאֵל הָיְתָה.

messages.text: Chapter 2 · יש בקרבנות · Yesh BaKorbanot: halakhot that apply to offerings of an individual and not to communal offerings, and the reverse. Chapter 1 ended on 13b.
Mishna

There are halakhot in effect with regard to offerings of an individual that are not in effect with regard to communal offerings; and there are halakhot in effect with regard to communal offerings that are not in effect with regard to offerings of an individual.

There are halakhot in effect with regard to offerings of an individual that are not in effect with regard to communal offerings, as offerings of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for the offering a substitute, and communal offerings do not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for the offering a substitute.
Offerings of an individual apply to, i.e., can be brought from, both males and females, but communal offerings apply only to males.

notes.he: כולם זכרים דרובן עולות ועולה זכר הוא ואין ציבור מביאין שלמים אלא כבשי עצרת דזכרים הן וחטאות שלהן שעירים כדכתיב בכולהו ושעיר חטאת אחד:
notes.en: Mishna. Communal offerings: They are all males, since most of them are burnt offerings, and a burnt offering is a male. And the community brings no peace offerings except the lambs of Shavuot [Atzeret], which are males. And their sin offerings are goats, as is written with regard to all of them: “And one goat for a sin offering.”

messages.text: If offerings of an individual were not brought at the appropriate time, one is obligated to bring their compensation and compensation for their accompanying meal offering and libations at a later date, but if communal offerings were not brought at the appropriate time, one is obligated to bring neither their compensation nor compensation for their accompanying meal offering and libations at a later date.

notes.he: כלומר יש מהן מאותן שקבוע להן זמן שאפי' עבר זמנם חייבין להקריבן כגון קרבן עולת יולדת (וקרבנה) וקרבנות מצורע אם עבר שמיני שלו יכול להקריבו לאחר זמן אבל קרבנות ציבור שיש להן זמן אם עבר זמנם בטל קרבנן כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Offerings of an individual: one is obligated to bring their compensation: That is, some of them, among those that have a fixed time, even if their time has passed one is obligated to sacrifice them, for example the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth, and the offerings of a leper: if his eighth day has passed, he can sacrifice it after its time. But communal offerings that have a set time, if their time has passed, their offering is void, as is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: But one is obligated to bring compensation for their accompanying meal offering and libations once the offering is sacrificed.

notes.he: שאם קרב הזבח בזמנו ולא קרבו נסכים עמו חייבין להקריבם אפי' מכאן ועד עשרה ימים כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Once the offering is sacrificed: That if the offering was sacrificed at its time and the libations were not sacrificed with it, one is obligated to sacrifice them, even ten days from now, as is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: There are halakhot in effect with regard to communal offerings that are not in effect with regard to offerings of an individual, as communal offerings override Shabbat, in that they are sacrificed on Shabbat, and they override ritual impurity, i.e., they are sacrificed even if the priests are impure with impurity imparted by a corpse; and offerings of an individual override neither Shabbat nor ritual impurity.

But aren’t the High Priest’s griddle-cake offerings and the bull of Yom Kippur offerings of an individual, and yet they override Shabbat and ritual impurity. Rather, this is the principle: Any offering, individual or communal, whose time is fixed overrides Shabbat and ritual impurity, whereas any offering, individual or communal, whose time is not fixed overrides neither Shabbat nor ritual impurity.
messages.quote: offerings of an individual override neither Shabbat nor ritual impurity

notes.he: דוחין שבת וטומאה דכתיב בה מנחה תמיד הרי היא לך כמנחת תמידין בשילהי [התכלת] במנחות (דף נ:):
notes.en: The High Priest’s griddle-cake offerings: They override Shabbat and impurity, as it is written of them: “A meal offering perpetually [tamid]” [Leviticus 6:13]; it is like the meal offering of the daily offerings [temidin], [as stated] at the end of [the chapter] HaTekhelet in Menaḥot (50b).

notes.he: פרו של אהרן:
notes.en: The bull of Yom Kippur: The bull of Aaron [i.e., of the High Priest].

notes.he: כלומר אין הטעם תלוי אלא בקביעות זמן אותן שזמנן קבוע שאם עבר הזמן אין להן תשלומין דוחין שבת וטומאה אפילו דיחיד וכל שאין להן זמן קבוע אינם דוחין שבת וטומאה ואפי' דציבור כגון פר העלם דבר של ציבור ושעירי עבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: Rather, whose time is fixed: That is, the reason depends only on the fixing of the time. Those whose time is fixed, which have no compensation if the time has passed, override Shabbat and impurity, even those of an individual; and all those that have no fixed time do not override Shabbat and impurity, even communal ones, for example the bull for an unwitting communal sin [he’elem davar shel tzibbur] and the goats for idol worship.

notes.he: אמר רבי מאיר והלא חביתי כו' אלא שזמנן קבוע כלומר קסבר ר' מאיר אין הפרש ביניהן דכל שזמנו קבוע בין ביחיד בין בצבור דוחה את השבת ואת הטומאה:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir said: But aren’t the griddle-cake offerings, etc. Rather, whose time is fixed: That is, Rabbi Meir holds there is no difference between them: any offering whose time is fixed, whether of an individual or of the community, overrides Shabbat and impurity.

messages.caption: The mishna’s differences between offerings of an individual and communal offerings, with Rabbi Meir’s principle of a fixed time.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that offerings of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for the offering a substitute. And is this an established principle? Does every offering of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute? But what about birds, i.e., a dove or a pigeon, which are brought as an offering of an individual, but they do not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for them a substitute?
messages.quote: offerings of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for the offering a substitute

messages.text: When the mishna teaches that offerings of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for the offering a substitute, it is teaching this only with regard to an animal offering, not a bird offering.

But what about the offspring of a sanctified animal, which is brought and sacrificed on the altar as an offering of an individual of the same type as its mother, and yet it does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute?

notes.dh: [והרי וולד דקרבן יחיד ואין עשה תמורה
notes.he: כדאמר בפרקין דלעיל והיה הוא ולא ולד:
notes.en: But there is the offspring of an individual’s offering, and it does not render a substitute: As it says in the previous chapter: “It” [Leviticus 27:10: “then it and its substitute shall be sacred”], and not the offspring.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this mishna? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that the offspring of a sanctified animal renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.

notes.he: הא מני מתניתין דקתני דקרבנות יחיד עושין תמורה דאפי' ולד דקרבן יחיד ר' יהודה היא:
notes.en: In accordance with whose opinion is the mishna, which teaches that offerings of an individual render a substitute, even the offspring of an individual’s offering? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: But what about a substitute itself, which is brought and sacrificed on the altar as an offering of an individual, and yet a substitute does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute?

When the mishna teaches that an offering of an individual renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute, it is teaching this only with regard to the primary offering, not a substitute of an offering.

notes.he: הקדש ראשון:
notes.en: Gemara. The primary offering: The first consecrated animal.

notes.dh: והא תמורה דקרבן יחיד ואין עושה תמורה אחרת
notes.he: כדאמר לעיל ולא תמורת תמורתו כי קתני דקרבנות יחיד עושין תמורה בעיקר זיבחא גופיה קתני ולא בתמורה ולא בולד:
notes.en: But there is the substitute of an individual’s offering, and it does not render another substitute: As it says above: “And not the substitute of its substitute.” When it teaches that offerings of an individual render a substitute, it teaches it of the primary offering itself, and not of a substitute nor of offspring.

messages.text: Now that you have arrived at this answer, you can even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda and maintain that the offspring of an offering does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute. The reason is that one can explain that the mishna is teaching its halakha only with regard to the primary offering, not the offspring of an offering.
messages.quote: with regard to the primary offering

notes.he: דלית להו ולד עושה תמורה:
notes.en: You can even say it is the Rabbis: Who do not hold that the offspring renders a substitute.

notes.dh: והשתא דאתית להכי אפי' תימא מתניתין רבנן היא
notes.he: ודקשיא והרי ולד דקרבן יחיד ואין עושה תמורה כי קתני מתני' בעיקר זיבחא דיחיד קתני דעושה תמורה:
notes.en: And now that you have arrived at this, you can even say the mishna is the Rabbis. And as for the difficulty, “But there is the offspring of an individual’s offering and it does not render a substitute”: when the mishna teaches, it teaches of the primary offering of an individual, that it renders a substitute.

messages.text: § Is this an established principle, that all offerings of an individual may be brought from either a male or female animal? But what about a burnt offering, which is an offering of an individual, and yet it comes as a male animal but does not come as a female animal.
messages.quote: Offerings of an individual apply to, i.e., can be brought from, both males and females

notes.he: משמע כל קרבן שחייב היחיד להביא בין זכר בין נקבה:
notes.en: Both males and females: This implies that every offering that an individual is obligated to bring [may come] either as a male or as a female.

messages.text: There is a bird burnt offering, i.e., there is a type of burnt offering that can be either a female or male bird.

notes.he: תירוצא הוא:
notes.en: There is the bird burnt offering: This is an answer.

notes.he: דאפי' נקבה אתיא והיינו פירוקא:
notes.en: But there is the bird burnt offering: Which comes even as a female; and this is the answer.

messages.text: The requirement of unblemished status and the requirement of male status both apply to a sacrificial animal brought as a burnt offering, but the requirement of unblemished status and the requirement of male status do not apply to sacrificial birds brought as burnt offerings.
But what about a sin offering, which is an offering of an individual, and yet comes as a female animal but does not come as a male animal.
There is the goat sin offering of a king, which is sacrificed by a specific individual and is brought specifically as a male animal.

notes.he: דנשיא דהיינו דיחיד דזכר הוא והאי נמי פירוקא:
notes.en: But there is the goat sin offering: of a king, which is an individual’s, and it is a male; and this too is an answer.

messages.text: But there is the individual guilt offering, which comes as a male animal but does not come as a female animal.

notes.he: הוי זכר דכבש או איל כתיב ביה ולא כבשה:
notes.en: A guilt offering: It is a male, since “a lamb” or “a ram” is written with regard to it, and not a ewe.

notes.he: דקרבן יחיד זכר אתי ולא נקבה:
notes.en: But there is the guilt offering: An individual’s offering that comes as a male and not as a female.

messages.text: When the Sages stated this halakha in the mishna they were referring only to an offering that is equivalent, i.e., which is brought both as an offering of an individual and as a communal offering, whereas a guilt offering is brought as an offering of an individual but is not brought as a communal offering.

Does the mishna teach: All offerings may be brought as either male or female? It does not. Rather, the mishna teaches: There are offerings of an individual that may be brought as male or female; and what are they? Peace offerings; and in the case of such an offering, if one wants he brings a female animal and if he wants he brings a male animal.
messages.lead: And if you wish, say instead an alternative explanation:

notes.he: אבל שלמי צבור זכרים הם דכתיב בהו (ויקרא כ״ג:י״ט) ושני כבשים בני שנה לזבח שלמים. זבחי שלמי צבור כבשי עצרת:
notes.en: What are they? Peace offerings: But communal peace offerings are males, as it is written of them: “And two male lambs in their first year as a sacrifice of peace offerings” (Leviticus 23:19). The communal peace offerings are the lambs of Shavuot [Atzeret].

messages.text: § From where do we derive this halakha, that if a communal offering was not sacrificed at the appropriate time it is not brought at a later stage?
messages.quote: If offerings of an individual were not brought at the appropriate time, one is obligated to bring their compensation

notes.he: דקרבנות צבור אין להן תשלומין:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: That communal offerings have no compensation.

notes.he: דקרבן צבור אין חייבין באחריותו]:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: That one is not obligated to bring compensation for a communal offering.

messages.text: The verse states in the section of the Torah dealing with additional offerings: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to bring an offering made by fire to the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meal offering, a sacrifice, and libations, each day on its own day” (Leviticus 23:37). This teaches that the entire day is fit for bringing the additional offerings.

verse.he: אֵלֶּה מוֹעֲדֵי יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר־תִּקְרְאוּ אֹתָם מִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ לְהַקְרִיב אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה עֹלָה וּמִנְחָה זֶבַח וּנְסָכִים דְּבַר־יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ׃
verse.en: Those are the set times of GOD that you shall celebrate as sacred occasions, bringing offerings by fire to GOD—burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and libations, on each day what is proper to it—

notes.he: במוספי המועדים משתעי בפרשת שור או כשב דכתיב אלה מועדי ה' מקראי קדש וגו' להקריב אשה ואיזה אשה מקריבין במועד יותר משאר ימים הוי אומר מוספין:
notes.en: Each day on its own day: It speaks of the additional offerings of the Festivals, in the section “An ox or a sheep” [Leviticus 22:27 and on], as it is written: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, holy convocations, etc., to bring an offering made by fire.” And which offering made by fire does one sacrifice on a Festival beyond other days? You must say: the additional offerings.

notes.he: ובלבד שיקדמו מוספין לתמיד של בין הערבים דאמר (ביומא דף לג.) עליה השלם כל הקרבנות כולן:
notes.en: That the entire day is fit for the additional offerings: Provided that the additional offerings precede the afternoon daily offering, as it says (Yoma 33a): “Upon it complete all the offerings” [i.e., the afternoon daily offering concludes the day’s service].

notes.dh: דת"ר אלה מועדי ה' מקראי קדש להקריב אשה לה' עולה ומנחה זבח ונסכים דבר יום ביומו
notes.he: [דבר יום] מלמד שכל היום כשר למוספין דהיינו עולה [היינו מוספין]:
notes.en: As the Sages taught: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, holy convocations, to bring an offering made by fire to the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meal offering, a sacrifice, and libations, each day on its own day.” “Each day” teaches that the entire day is fit for the additional offerings; that is, “a burnt offering” means the additional offerings.

messages.text: The term: “On its own day,” teaches that if the day has passed and the priests did not bring the additional offerings, one is not obligated to bring their compensation, and the offering cannot be brought at a later date.

notes.he: מלמד שאם עבר [היום ולא הביאן אין חייב באחריותן] דביומו [משמע דוקא ביומו] (כתב כלומר) הא אם עבר יומו בטל קרבנו [ואינו חייב באחריותן:
notes.en: “On its own day” teaches that if the day has passed and he did not bring them, he is not obligated to bring their compensation, since “on its own day” implies specifically on its own day. Thus if its day has passed, its offering is void and he is not obligated to bring their compensation.

messages.text: One might have thought that one should not be obligated to bring compensation for their accompanying libations at a later date even if the additional offering has been sacrificed, e.g., if there were no meal offerings or libations available at that time. Therefore, the verse states, in the chapter dealing with the additional offerings of the Festivals: “Their meal offerings and their libations” (Numbers 29:37).

verse.he: מִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם לַפָּר לָאַיִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂים בְּמִסְפָּרָם כַּמִּשְׁפָּט׃
verse.en: the grain offerings and libations for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, in the quantities prescribed;

messages.text: It is derived from here that the meal offerings and libations which are brought with the additional animal offerings of the Festivals can be sacrificed even in the night after the animal offering. The phrase “their meal offerings and their libations” further teaches that these meal offerings and libations can be sacrificed even on the following day.

notes.dh: מנחתם ונסכיהם אפי' בלילה ואפי' למחר
notes.he: אם קרב הקרבן בזמנו ואפי' מכאן ועד עשרה ימים ולעולם ובלא נזדמנו לו קא מיירי:
notes.en: Their meal offerings and their libations, even at night and even on the morrow: If the offering was sacrificed at its time, [the libations may be brought] even ten days from now, and indefinitely. And it is speaking of a case where they were not available to him [at the time].

messages.text: The source is from the following verse: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to bring an offering made by fire unto the Lord…each on its own day; beside the Shabbatot of the Lord” (Leviticus 23:37–38). The verse is expounded as speaking of a Festival that occurred on a Sunday, and therefore it is teaching that the meal offerings and libations for the additional offerings of the previous Shabbat may be brought on the following Festival day.

verse.he: מִלְּבַד שַׁבְּתֹת יְהֹוָה וּמִלְּבַד מַתְּנוֹתֵיכֶם וּמִלְּבַד כׇּל־נִדְרֵיכֶם וּמִלְּבַד כׇּל־נִדְבֹתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר תִּתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: apart from the sabbaths of GOD, and apart from your gifts and from all your votive offerings and from all your freewill offerings that you give to GOD.

notes.he: דהכי כתי' זבח ונסכים דבר יום ביומו מלבד שבתות ה' ומשום דדרשינן סמוכים דבר יום ביומו הקרב נסכים מלבד אותן של שבתות דאם יו"ט אחר שבת הוא הקרב נסכיו עם קרבנותיו והקרב נסכים ששכחת אתמול ולא הקרבת:
notes.en: Beside the Shabbatot of the Lord: For so it is written: “A sacrifice and libations, each day on its own day; beside the Shabbatot of the Lord.” And because we expound juxtaposed verses: “each day on its own day,” sacrifice libations, besides those of the Shabbatot; that is, if a Festival falls after Shabbat, sacrifice its libations with its offerings, and sacrifice the libations that you forgot yesterday and did not sacrifice.

notes.he: אף משקרב הזבח ת"ל בפרשת פנחס ומנחתם ונסכיהם ריבה דאפי' בלילה ואפי' למחר משום דחייב באחריותן] ריש לקיש אמר [מהכא] (מה בא) דחייב באחריות [משקרב הזבח] מדסמוך ליה מלבד שבתות ה' דמשמע דאי הוי י"ט אחר השבת [ולא הקריבו נסכי המוספין של שבת בשבת מביאין עכשו בי"ט דכתיב זבח ונסכים דבר יום ביומו מלבד שבתות ה' כלומר דשל י"ט קרבי והני של אתמול של שבת היינו מלבד שבתות ה' אלמא ונסכיהם אף למחר:
notes.en: One might have thought he is not obligated to bring compensation for their libations even once the offering has been sacrificed; the verse states in the section of Pinḥas: “And their meal offerings and their libations,” including even at night and even on the morrow, since he is obligated to bring their compensation. Reish Lakish says [it is derived from here] that he is obligated to bring compensation [once the offering has been sacrificed]: from the fact that “beside the Shabbatot of the Lord” is juxtaposed to it. This implies that if a Festival fell after Shabbat, [and they did not sacrifice the libations of the additional offerings of Shabbat on Shabbat,] they bring them now, on the Festival, as it is written: “A sacrifice and libations, each day on its own day; beside the Shabbatot of the Lord.” That is, those of the Festival are sacrificed, and these of yesterday, of Shabbat, are “beside the Shabbatot of the Lord.” Evidently “and their libations” [applies] even on the morrow.

messages.text: And both verses are necessary, as if the Merciful One had written only the verse: “Beside the Shabbatot of the Lord,” I would say that on the day following Shabbat, yes, one may bring the offerings, but on the night after Shabbat, no, one may not bring them, just as the offering itself could not have been brought at night. Therefore, the verse states: “And their meal offerings and their libations.”

notes.he: דהא דבר יום ביומו כתיב וסמיך ליה מלבד שבתות ה' כלומר נסכי השבת תקריב היום ביו"ט אבל בלילה לא:
notes.en: On the day, yes; at night, no: For “each day on its own day” is written, and juxtaposed to it is “beside the Shabbatot of the Lord.” That is, sacrifice the libations of Shabbat today, on the Festival, but not at night.

messages.text: And if the Merciful One had written only: “Their meal offerings and their libations,” and not written: “Beside the Shabbatot of the Lord,” I would say that at night, yes, the offerings may be brought, but on the following day they may not be brought.

notes.dh: ואי כתב מנחתם ונסכיהם הוה אמינא
notes.he: ללמדך שתקריב נסכי היום בלילה הבא אבל ביממא דלמחר לא:
notes.en: And if it had written “their meal offerings and their libations,” I would say: [It comes] to teach you that you may sacrifice the libations of the day on the night that follows, but not on the following day.

messages.text: And in what way is the night different from the day, that one might have thought the outstanding meal offerings and libations may be brought only at night but not during the day? One might have thought so because with regard to sacrificial animals and offerings the night follows the day. Therefore, the Torah had to teach that the meal offering and libations may be brought even the following day. Indeed both verses are necessary.
messages.quote: at night, yes, … but on the following day they may not be brought

notes.he: כלומר וכי תימא מאי שנא דלימא בלילה אין ביממא לא הא קרא סתמא הוה כתיב:
notes.en: And what is different: That is, and if you would say: Why should it be different, that one would say at night, yes, by day, no? The verse is written without qualification.

notes.dh: משום דבקדשים הלילה הולך אחר היום
notes.he: שעבר דכתיב (ויקרא ז) ביום קרבנו יאכל לא תותירו ממנו עד בקר אלמא כל הלילה קרי יום קרבנו הלכך סד"א בלילה יקרב דהנסכים הוי מיום שעבר אבל ביממא דלמחר לא:
notes.en: Because with regard to sacrificial animals the night follows the day: that has passed, as it is written: “On the day of his offering it shall be eaten; you shall not leave any of it until the morning” (Leviticus 7:15). Evidently it calls the whole night “the day of his offering.” Therefore it might enter your mind that at night it may be sacrificed, since the libations are [still considered] of the day that passed, but not on the following day.

notes.he: בלילה (באין) [הוא] דקרבי ולא לאחר משום] דבקדשים לילה הולך אחר היום דכתיב ומיום השמיני והלאה ירצה (דכל לילה) [כלומר דבליל שמיני] אסור לשוחטו דאותו לילה משלימין אחר שבעת ימים במחוסר זמן דבקדשים לילה הולך אחר היום [להכי הדר כתב מלבד שבתות ה' גבי ביומו למימרא דלמחר אייתי נסכים דאתמול דביו"ט מקריב נסכים של שבת. מבוא השמש משתשקע החמה]:
notes.en: And if you would say, what is different, [that it is at night] that they are sacrificed and not afterward? Because with regard to sacrificial animals the night follows the day, as it is written: “And from the eighth day and onward it shall be accepted” [Leviticus 22:27]; [that is, on the night of the eighth] it is forbidden to slaughter it, since that night completes the seven days [and the animal is still premature]. With regard to a premature animal, then, the night follows the day in sacrificial matters. [Therefore it wrote again “beside the Shabbatot of the Lord” with “on its own day,” to say that on the morrow one brings yesterday’s libations: on the Festival one sacrifices the libations of Shabbat. “After sunset” means once the sun has set.]

messages.text: And libations, may they be sacrificed at night? Didn’t we learn in a baraita:
messages.quote: can be sacrificed even in the night

messages.text: I have derived only with regard to items that are normally sacrificed at night, for example, the limbs of a burnt offering and the fats of burnt offerings and other offerings, that one sacrifices them after sunset and they are consumed throughout the entire night. This is derived from the verse: “This is the law of the burnt offering: It is that which goes up on its firewood upon the altar all night unto the morning” (Leviticus 6:2).

verse.he: צַו אֶת־אַהֲרֹן וְאֶת־בָּנָיו לֵאמֹר זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעֹלָה הִוא הָעֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָהֿ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ כׇּל־הַלַּיְלָה עַד־הַבֹּקֶר וְאֵשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ תּוּקַד בּוֹ׃
verse.en:
Command Aaron and his sons thus:
This is the ritual of the burnt offering: The burnt offering itself shall remain where it is burned upon the altar all night until morning, while the fire on the altar is kept going on it.

notes.he: בת"כ היא ואקרא קאי דכתיב היא העולה על מוקדה על המזבח כל הלילה שיהא נותנן מבוא השמש ומתעכלין כל הלילה:
notes.en: I have only, etc.: It is in Torat Kohanim [the Sifra], and refers to the verse that is written: “It is that which goes up on its firewood upon the altar all night,” that one places them from sunset and they are consumed all night.

notes.dh: אין לי אלא דברים שדרכן ליקרב בלילה כגון
notes.he: אברים דעולה ופדרים כדרבי להו לעיל שיהא נותנן מבוא השמש כלומר לאחר שקיעת החמה נותנן על המערכה:
notes.en: I have only items that are normally sacrificed at night, for example: The limbs of a burnt offering and the fats, which were included above for this, that one places them from sunset, that is, after the setting of the sun one places them on the arrangement of wood.

messages.text: But with regard to items that are normally sacrificed in the day, for example the handful of the meal offering, and the frankincense, and the meal offering that accompanies the libations, from where is it derived that one may bring them up and burn them after sunset?

notes.he: דאינן קריבין בלילה כלל דכולהו קרבנות כתיב בהו ביום צוותו דמשמע ביום ולא בלילה אבל אברים ופדרים הוא דאיתרבו הכא בלילה מהאי קרא שמקריבין מבוא השמש וקא מקטירן על המערכה והם מתעכלין מאיליהן דאם לא כן היא העולה מאי ממעט:
notes.en: Items that are normally sacrificed in the day: Which are not sacrificed at night at all, since with regard to all the offerings it is written: “On the day that he commanded” [Leviticus 7:38], which implies by day and not at night. But limbs and fats are what is included here, at night, by this verse: that one sacrifices them from sunset and burns them on the arrangement of wood, and they are consumed by themselves. For if not so, what would “it is the burnt offering” exclude?

messages.text: Would it enter your mind that they may be burned after sunset? But didn’t you say that these are items that are normally sacrificed in the day? Rather, the question of the baraita is as follows: From where is it derived that these items may be sacrificed with sunset, i.e., just before sunset, in which case they are consumed throughout the entire night and not during the day?
messages.quote: that one may bring them up and burn them after sunset

notes.he: ופריך מבוא השמש והאמרת דרכו ליקרב ביום:
notes.en: And he asks: After sunset? But you said it is normally sacrificed in the day!

notes.he: קודם שקיעה:
notes.en: Rather, with sunset: Before the sun sets.

notes.he: היינו סמוך קוד' שתשקע החמה:
notes.en: Until sunset [ad bo hashemesh; the Gemara reads “with sunset”]: That is, close to, before the sun sets.

messages.text: The verse states: “This is the law of the burnt offering” (Leviticus 6:2), a phrase that included everything sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: כל העולין:
notes.en: “This is the law of the burnt offering” included: all that go up [on the altar].

messages.text: In any event, the baraita teaches that the meal offering that accompanies the libations is brought only in the day, not at night.

This is not difficult. Here, where the verse states: “Their meal offerings and libations,” it is referring to consecrating the offering if one placed it in a consecrated utensil at night. The offering becomes consecrated and may not be used for non-sacred purposes. There, in the verse cited by the baraita as teaching that it may be brought only in the day and not at night, it is referring to sacrificing the offering on the altar. Even if an offering was consecrated at night, it may not be sacrificed until the following morning.

notes.he: בלילה אם ניתנו בכלי שרת קדשי דתו לא נפקי לחולין אבל מיקרב לא קרבי עד היום:
notes.en: To consecrate: At night, if they were placed in a service vessel they are consecrated, so they can no longer go out to non-sacred status; but as for being sacrificed, they are not sacrificed until the day.

notes.he: כאן ליקדש כאן ליקרב ליקדש מקדישין נסכים אפי' בלילה אבל מיקרב אין מקריבין אלא ביום. אמר רבא ואי מקדש קדשי בלילה קרבי נמי קרבי דהא תניא זה הכלל כו':
notes.en: Here to consecrate, there to sacrifice: To consecrate, one consecrates libations even at night; but to sacrifice, one sacrifices only by day. Rava said: And if they are consecrated at night, they are also sacrificed [at night], as it is taught: This is the principle, etc.

messages.text: @Rami bar Ḥama If the meal offering accompanying the libations can be consecrated at night, it should also be fit to be sacrificed at night. No distinction can be made between consecrating and sacrificing, as isn’t it taught in a baraita:

notes.he: בלילה מיקרב נמי קרבי:
notes.en: If they are consecrated: at night, they are also sacrificed [at night].

messages.text: This is the principle: Any offering that is sacrificed in the day is consecrated only in the day; and any offering that is sacrificed at night is consecrated only at night; and any offering that is sacrificed both in the day and at night is consecrated both in the day and at night.

notes.he: פרש"י שילהי שתי הלחם (מנחות דף ק.) כגון שמן למנורה ולא נראה דמה קדושה שייכי ביה הא לית ביה קדושת כלי לכך נראה לומר דלא מצינו קרב בלילה אלא מנחת נסכים ומשו"ה ניחא דלא משני הכא דילמא אינו קדוש ליקדש אבל קדוש ליפסל דהכי מסיק התם שילהי פ' שתי הלחם (גז"ש) דסמיך אהא דתני וכל הקרב בלילה דלא מצינו קרב בלילה אלא מנחת נסכים בלבד וה"ה דמצי למיפרך מינה הכא בהדיא מדקתני וכל הקרב בלילה ולא מצינו דבר זה אלא מנחת נסכים בלבד אלא דמהדר לפרוכי אף לפי מה דס"ד מעיקרא התם בפ' שתי הלחם:
notes.en: And any that is sacrificed at night: Rashi explained at the end of [the chapter] Shetei HaLeḥem (Menaḥot 100a): for example, oil for the Candelabrum. But this does not seem right, for what sanctity applies to it? It has no sanctity of a vessel. Therefore it seems one should say that we find nothing sacrificed at night except the meal offering that accompanies libations. And because of this it is understandable that [the Gemara] does not answer here: Perhaps it is not consecrated so as to be sacrificed, but it is consecrated so as to become disqualified; for so it concludes there, at the end of the chapter Shetei HaLeḥem, relying on what is taught: “And any that is sacrificed at night,” since we find nothing sacrificed at night except the meal offering of libations alone. And by the same token [the Gemara] could have raised the difficulty from it here explicitly, from the fact that it teaches: “And any that is sacrificed at night,” and we find this only with the meal offering of libations; but it prefers to raise the difficulty even according to what was initially assumed there in the chapter Shetei HaLeḥem.

messages.text: The meal offering accompanying the libations may be sacrificed at night, and therefore one should delete from this baraita the item: Meal offering that accompanies the libations, from the list of the offerings that may not be brought at night.

notes.he: לא תימני להו עם דברים שדרכן ליקרב ביום:
notes.en: Delete the libations from here: Do not count them with the items that are normally sacrificed in the day.

notes.dh: אלא סמי מן ההיא מתניתא דאין לי
notes.he: מנחת נסכין משום דהא קרבי נמי בלילה]:
notes.en: Rather, delete from that baraita of “I have only” the meal offering of libations, because it is also sacrificed at night.

messages.text: When Rav Dimi ascended from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, he found Rav Yirmeya sitting and saying in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

From where is it derived that libations that come with an animal offering may be sacrificed only in the day? The verse states: “These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed seasons, beside your vows, and your voluntary offerings, and your burnt offerings, and your meal offerings, and your libations, and your peace offerings” (Numbers 29:39). The juxtaposition of these two items teaches that just as peace offerings may be sacrificed only during the day, so too libations may be sacrificed only during the day.
messages.lead: Rav Yirmeya, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

verse.he: אֵלֶּה תַּעֲשׂוּ לַיהֹוָה בְּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם לְעֹלֹתֵיכֶם וּלְמִנְחֹתֵיכֶם וּלְנִסְכֵּיכֶם וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: All these you shall offer to GOD at the stated times, in addition to your votive and freewill offerings, be they burnt offerings, grain offerings, libations, or offerings of well-being.

notes.he: שמביאין עם הזבח וקידשן שחיטת הזבח דהוי כי זבח גופיה ואינן קריבין אלא ביום:
notes.en: With the offering: That are brought with the offering, and the slaughter of the offering consecrated them, so that they are like the offering itself, and they are sacrificed only by day.

messages.text: If I find someone who can write this opinion in a letter, I will send it to Rav Yosef in Babylonia,

notes.dh: אמר רב דימי אי אשכחיה אינשי כתיב איגרתא
notes.he: אם הייתי מוצא אדם הייתי כותב איגרתי והייתי שולח לרב יוסף לבבל:
notes.en: Rav Dimi said: If I would find someone who writes a letter: If I would find a person, I would write my letter and send it to Rav Yosef in Babylonia.

notes.he: אמר אי אשכחת איניש דאזיל להתם כתבי איגרת [ושדרית ליה (ע"כ שייך לע"א) דלא תיסמי מן מתניתא מנחת נסכין:
notes.en: When Rav Dimi ascended, etc.: He said: If I find someone who is going there, I will write a letter and send it to him, that he should not delete the meal offering of libations from the baraita.

messages.text: and in light of this ruling he will not delete the phrase: The meal offering that accompanies the libations, from the baraita.

notes.he: מההיא מתני' דלעיל ומצי לתרוצי:
notes.en: He will not delete the libations: from that baraita above, and he can answer:

messages.text: And instead, the apparent contradiction between the baraitot can be explained as follows: It is not difficult; here, the baraita that states that meal offerings accompanying libations are sacrificed only in the day is referring to libations that come with an animal offering, whereas there, the baraita that permits sacrificing a meal offering that accompanies the libations at night is referring to libations that come to be sacrificed by themselves, i.e., which do not accompany the sacrifice of an offering.

notes.he: דקתני נסכים בהדי דברים שדרכן ליקרב ביום היינו בנסכים הבאין עם הזבח:
notes.en: Here: That which teaches libations together with items that are normally sacrificed by day refers to libations that come with the offering.

notes.he: שלא קדשו בשחיטת הזבח יכול להקריב בלילה:
notes.en: By themselves: Which were not consecrated by the slaughter of the offering; one can sacrifice them at night.

notes.he: מתני' דקתני דמשקרב הזבח חייבין באחריותן כלומר אף בלילה ברייתא (דהא) דתני ומנחתם ונסכיהם בלילה היינו] בנסכים הבאין בפני עצמן. שלא הקדיש עם הזבח אלא שהקדישום לאחר הקרבת הזבח שיכול אדם להקריב זבחו היום ונסכיו מיכן ועד עשרה ימים ובהנהו אמר דקרבי [אף] בלילה [והא דקתני ברייתא דברים שדרכן להקריב ביום מנחת נסכים היינו בנסכים הבאים עם הזבח]:
notes.en: And it is not difficult: The mishna teaches that once the offering has been sacrificed one is obligated to bring compensation for them, that is, even at night; and the baraita that teaches “and their meal offerings and their libations,” at night, refers to libations that come by themselves: he did not consecrate them with the offering, but consecrated them after the sacrifice of the offering, since a person can sacrifice his offering today and its libations even ten days from now; and of these it says that they are sacrificed even at night. And what the baraita teaches among items normally sacrificed by day, the meal offering of libations, refers to libations that come with the offering.

messages.text: And even if he had someone to write a letter for him, would it have been possible to send it? But didn’t Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, say that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
messages.quote: If I find someone who can write this opinion in a letter

messages.text: Those who write halakhot are considered like those who burn the Torah, and one who learns from written halakhot does not receive the reward of studying Torah.

notes.he: שאין מצילין אותן בשבת בפני הדליקה. ל"א שאסור להשהותן כתובים דתורה שבעל פה היא:
notes.en: Like those who burn the Torah: For they are not rescued from a fire on Shabbat. Another explanation: Because it is forbidden to keep them written, since it is the Oral Torah.

notes.he: מתוך הספרים:
notes.en: And one who learns from them: From the books.

notes.he: מדרש משנה ותלמוד והגדות [דברים שבע"פ נענשין] כשורפי תורה משום דדינן של הלכות בע"פ ואינו רשאי לכותבן [וכל הלמד מהן מן הכתב אין לו שכר:
notes.en: Those who write halakhot: The midrash of the Mishna, and Talmud and aggadot, [matters of the Oral Law; they are punished] like those who burn the Torah, because the law is that halakhot are oral and one is not permitted to write them. And anyone who learns from them, from writing, has no reward.

messages.text: Evidently, it is prohibited to send halakhot in letters.

One verse says: “Write you these words,” and one verse says, i.e., it states later in that same verse: “For by the mouth of these words” (Exodus 34:27). These phrases serve to say to you: Words that were taught orally you may not recite in writing, and words that are written you may not recite orally, i.e., by heart.
messages.lead: Before resolving the difficulty, the Gemara further discusses the prohibition of writing down the Torah: Rabbi Yehuda bar Naḥmani, the disseminator for Reish Lakish, expounded as follows:

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה כְּתׇב־לְךָ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה כִּי עַל־פִּי ׀ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה כָּרַתִּי אִתְּךָ בְּרִית וְאֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: And GOD said to Moses: Write down these commandments, for in accordance with these commandments I make a covenant with you and with Israel.

notes.dh: דברים שבכתב אי אתה רשאי לאומרם בעל פה
notes.he: וא"ת היכי קאמרינן מזמורים על פה וי"ל דאין להקפיד רק מה שכתוב בחומש אמנם קשה היכי קרינן ויושע וקריאת שמע וי"ל דאין להקפיד אלא בדבר שמוציא אחרים ידי חובתן:
notes.en: Words that are written you may not recite orally: And if you will say: How do we recite psalms by heart? One can say that one need be particular only about what is written in the Pentateuch. However, it is difficult: How do we recite “And He saved” [the Song of the Sea] and the Shema [by heart]? One can say that one need be particular only about something with which one fulfills the obligation of others.

messages.text: The word “these” in the command “write you these words” serves to emphasize that these words, i.e., those recorded in the Written Law, you may write, but you may not write halakhot, i.e., the mishnayot and the rest of the Oral Law.
messages.lead: And furthermore, the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

messages.text: Perhaps with regard to a new matter it is different, i.e., it might be permitted to write down new material so that it not be forgotten.
messages.lead: They said in response to the question of how Rav Dimi could propose writing down the halakha in a letter:

notes.he: חדשה שלא היו יודעין לתרץ הברייתות:
notes.en: New [ḥadta]: A new matter, in that they did not know how to resolve the baraitot.

notes.he: לחדש דבר כגון זו שחדשה היא:
notes.en: [Another version:] Ḥadtei: To innovate something, such as this one, which is new.

notes.he: תורה נביאים וכתובים. חדושי מילתא שאני. דבר חדוש הוה אותו היקישא ומשום הכי מותר:
notes.en: Words that are written: The Torah, Prophets and Writings. A new matter is different: That juxtaposition was a new matter, and therefore it is permitted [to write it].

messages.text: One proof for this suggestion is that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish would read from a scroll of aggada, containing the words of the Sages, on Shabbat.

notes.he: שלא ישתכחו:
notes.en: Read from a scroll of aggada: So that they would not be forgotten.

notes.he: ל"א משום דאיכא שכחה כתבין ואמאי מותר]:
notes.en: Another version: Because there is [a concern of] forgetting, they write; and why is it permitted?

messages.text: And they did so because they taught as follows: Since one cannot remember the Oral Law without writing it down, it is permitted to violate the halakha, as derived from the verse: “It is time to work for the Lord; they have made void your Torah” (Psalms 119:126). They said it is better to uproot a single halakha of the Torah, i.e., the prohibition of writing down the Oral Torah, and thereby ensure that the Torah is not forgotten from the Jewish people entirely.

verse.en:
It is a time to act for GOD,
for they have violated Your teaching.

notes.he: כשעושין הדבר לשם קדושת השם ראוי להפר תורתך ומוטב תעקר כו':
notes.en: It is time to work for the Lord: When one does something for the sake of sanctifying God’s name, it is fitting to make void Your Torah; and it is better that it be uprooted, etc.

notes.he: מוטב שתעקר [אות אחת מן התורה] דכתיב כי על פי ומוטב הוא לכתוב כדי שלא תשתכח תורה:
notes.en: Better that [one letter of the Torah] be uprooted, [the letter] where it is written “for by the mouth”; and it is better to write, so that the Torah not be forgotten.

messages.text: Now that you have said that libations that come by themselves are sacrificed even at night, if one happened to have libations of this kind at night, they may be consecrated by placing them in a service vessel at night and they may be sacrificed at night.
messages.lead: § With regard to Rav Dimi’s differentiation between libations that come with an animal offering and libations that are sacrificed by themselves:

notes.he: יכול להקדישן ולהקריבן בלילה אחת. ל"א גרסינן עלות השחר פוסל בהן כאברים כלומר הא דאמרינן נזדמנו לו נסכים בלילה מקדישן בלילה [ומקריבן]:
notes.en: Now that you have said, etc.: One can consecrate them and sacrifice them in one night. Another version: we read [here]: “Dawn disqualifies them, like limbs”; that is, as for what we said, that if libations happened to be available at night one consecrates them at night [and sacrifices them, dawn disqualifies them].

notes.he: השתא דאמרת נסכים הבאים בפני עצמן לאחר הקרבת הזבח [ומחמת] הזבח קריבין אפילו בלילה. אם נזדמנו לו מקדישן בלילה בכלי שרת ומקריבן בלילה דחייב באחריותן:
notes.en: Now that you have said that libations that come by themselves, after the sacrifice of the offering, [and on account of] the offering, are sacrificed even at night: If they happened to be available to him, he consecrates them at night in a service vessel and sacrifices them at night, since he is obligated to bring their compensation.

messages.text: @Rav Pappa A baraita is taught that supports your opinion.
messages.quote: consecrated by placing them in a service vessel at night

messages.text: This is the principle: Any offering that is sacrificed in the day is consecrated by being placed in a service vessel only in the day; but any offering that is sacrificed at night is consecrated both in the day and at night.

And dawn disqualifies them, like the halakha of limbs of offerings that have had their blood sprinkled during the day. Such limbs are left to burn on the altar all night long, but at dawn they are disqualified and may no longer be placed on the altar.
messages.lead: With regard to the topic of libations sacrificed by themselves:

notes.he: של תמיד במס' זבחים (פז.) וכן עיקר הגהת הרב:
notes.en: Like limbs: of the daily offering, in tractate Zevaḥim (87a). And this is the main version, the emendation of the Master.

notes.dh: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה עולת השחר
notes.he: התמיד פוסל בהן כאברין ואברייתא קאי דקתני ומתעכלין והולכין כל הלילה [כולה] (כלומר) ואם לא נתעכלו כל האברין של תמיד של בין הערבים עד שהעלו תמיד השחר פוסלת בהן באברים אבל סידור המערכה של תמיד השחר אינה פוסלת בהן אלא הקרבת [התמיד] עצמו דכבר הוי יום ואין דרכן ליקרב ביום:
notes.en: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: The dawn burnt offering [Rabbeinu Gershom reads olat, “burnt offering of,” for alot, “rising of”], i.e., the daily offering, disqualifies them like the limbs. And this refers to the baraita that teaches “and they are consumed throughout the entire night”: if all the limbs of the afternoon daily offering were not consumed by the time they offered up the morning daily offering, it disqualifies the limbs. But arranging the wood for the morning daily offering does not disqualify them; only the sacrifice of [the daily offering] itself, since it is already day and it is not their manner to be sacrificed by day.

messages.text: § The Gemara returns to discuss the verse: “These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed seasons, beside your vows, and your voluntary offerings, and your burnt offerings, and your meal offerings, and your libations, and your peace offerings” (Numbers 29:39).

verse.he: אֵלֶּה תַּעֲשׂוּ לַיהֹוָה בְּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם לְעֹלֹתֵיכֶם וּלְמִנְחֹתֵיכֶם וּלְנִסְכֵּיכֶם וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: All these you shall offer to GOD at the stated times, in addition to your votive and freewill offerings, be they burnt offerings, grain offerings, libations, or offerings of well-being.

messages.text: “These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed seasons,” i.e., these are the obligatory offerings that come to be sacrificed as obligatory offerings on the pilgrimage Festival, e.g., the burnt offerings of appearance, the Festival offerings, and the additional offerings.
messages.lead: When Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:

notes.he: כגון עולת ראיה וחגיגה ומוספין:
notes.en: Obligatory offerings that come on account of the pilgrimage Festival, on the Festival: For example, the burnt offering of appearance, the Festival peace offering, and the additional offerings.

messages.text: “Beside your vows and your voluntary offerings.” This teaches with regard to vows and voluntary offerings that they are sacrificed on the intermediate days of a Festival.

notes.dh: [לבד מנדריכם ונדבותיכ' לימד על נדר ונדבה] שקריבין בחולו של מועד
notes.he: נמי הוי (נמי) מועדיכם אבל בי"ט לא דנדר ונדבה אין קריבין בי"ט:
notes.en: [“Beside your vows and your voluntary offerings” teaches about vows and voluntary offerings] that they are sacrificed on the intermediate days of the Festival, which is also “your appointed seasons”; but not on the Festival day itself, for vows and voluntary offerings are not sacrificed on a Festival day.

messages.text: The verse further states: “And your burnt offerings.” With regard to what case is the verse speaking? If it is referring to a vow burnt offering, the verse already said: “Your vows.” And if it is referring to a voluntary burnt offering, the verse already said: “Your voluntary offerings.”

notes.he: אמור נדריכם:
notes.en: “Your vows” was already said.

messages.text: Consequently, it is speaking of nothing other than a burnt offering of a woman who gave birth, i.e., the lamb that she sacrifices on the forty-first day after giving birth to a son or the eighty-first day after giving birth to a daughter, and a burnt offering of a leper, which is the lamb that is sacrificed after a leper is purified. The verse teaches that these obligatory offerings may be sacrificed on the intermediate days of a Festival.

notes.dh: [הא אין הכתוב מדבר אלא בעולת יולדת
notes.he: ועולת מצורע דקרבי נמי בחולו של מועד:
notes.en: Consequently, the verse speaks only of the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth and the burnt offering of a leper, which are also sacrificed on the intermediate days of the Festival.

messages.text: The verse continues: “And your meal offerings.” With regard to what case is the verse speaking? If it is referring to a meal offering brought in fulfillment of a vow, the verse already said: “Your vows.” If it is referring to a voluntary meal offering, the verse already said: “Your voluntary offerings.” Consequently, it is speaking of nothing other than the meal offering of a sota, and that is the meal offering of jealousy.

notes.he: קרבי נמי בחולו של מועד:
notes.en: The sinner’s meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy [Rabbeinu Gershom names both; the daf names only the meal offering of a sota]: These too are sacrificed on the intermediate days of the Festival.

messages.text: “And your libations and your peace offerings.” The Torah here juxtaposes libations to peace offerings: Just as peace offerings are sacrificed only during the day, not at night, so too, libations are sacrificed only during the day, not at night.

notes.he: אף נסכים ביום:
notes.en: So too libations by day.

notes.he: אותן הבאין עם הזבח:
notes.en: So too libations by day: Those that come with the offering.

messages.text: “And your peace offerings.” This serves to include the peace offering of a nazirite, which he brings at the completion of his term of naziriteship. This offering may also be sacrificed on the intermediate days of a Festival.

notes.he: דאי שלמי נדבה הרי כבר אמור נדבותיכם ואי משום הקישא לכתוב ולשלמים:
notes.en: To include the peace offering of a nazirite: For if voluntary peace offerings [were meant], “your voluntary offerings” was already said; and if [it is written only] for the juxtaposition, let it write [simply] “and to the peace offerings.”

notes.he: דקרבי נמי בחולו של מועד:
notes.en: These are the nazirite’s peace offerings: Which are also sacrificed on the intermediate days of the Festival.

messages.caption: Numbers 29:39 phrase by phrase, as Rav Dimi reports it from Rabbi Yoḥanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak, with Abaye’s proposal.

messages.text: @Rav Dimi But let the Master say that the phrase “and your peace offerings” serves to include the peace offering that is brought together with a Paschal offering. This offering is sacrificed on the fourteenth of Nisan by a large group of people when they will not receive enough meat from their Paschal offering to feed them all. The suggested derivation from the verse is that if a peace offering separated for this purpose was not sacrificed on the fourteenth of Nisan, it may be brought during the intermediate days of the Festival.
messages.lead: With regard to the last halakha, when Rav Dimi cited this statement in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
messages.quote: to include the peace offering of a nazirite

notes.he: חגיגת י"ד שכשהיתה חבורה מרובה נמנים על הפסח ואינו סיפק להן היו מביאין עמו שלמים ואם הפרישן לשם כך ולא הקריבום יקריבום בחוה"מ דאי שלמי נזיר לא צריכי ריבוי לרבויי דמנדריכם ונדבותיכם נפקא דנזירות ע"י נדר בא עליו ונידר ונידב קרינא ביה אבל שלמי פסח חובה נינהו כדמפרש בפסחים בפ' ואלו דברים (דף עא.):
notes.en: Peace offerings of the Paschal offering: The Festival peace offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan]. When the group registered for the Paschal offering was large and it did not suffice for them, they would bring peace offerings with it. And if one separated them for this purpose and they did not sacrifice them, they sacrifice them on the intermediate days of the Festival. For the nazirite’s peace offerings do not need an inclusion, since they are derived from “your vows and your voluntary offerings”: naziriteship comes upon him through a vow, and it is called vowed and contributed. But the peace offerings of the Paschal offering are obligatory, as is explained in Pesaḥim, in the chapter Ve’elu Devarim (71a).

notes.he: שבאין חובה עם הפסח דכתב וזבחת שלמים ואכלת שם:
notes.en: And let the Master say: peace offerings of the Paschal offering, which come as an obligation with the Paschal offering, as it is written: “And you shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there” [Deuteronomy 27:7].

messages.text: It is more reasonable to include this peace offering, as, if the verse is referring to the peace offering of a nazirite, it is already included by the verse in the categories of offerings that are vowed or contributed voluntarily.

notes.dh: דאי שלמי נזיר דבר נידר ונידב הוא
notes.he: דנודר אדם להיות נזיר [ומונה נזירותו ומביא אח"כ שלמיו וכבר לימד על נדר ונדבה שקרב בחולו של מועד] א"כ ולשלמיכם תו למה לי:
notes.en: For if the nazirite’s peace offerings, it is something vowed and contributed: For a person vows to be a nazirite, counts his naziriteship and afterward brings his peace offerings, and it already taught about vows and voluntary offerings that they are sacrificed on the intermediate days. If so, why do I need “and your peace offerings”?

messages.text: As isn’t it taught in a baraita:

This is the principle: Any offering that is vowed or contributed voluntarily, e.g., a burnt offering or a peace offering, is sacrificed on a private altar. And any offering that is not vowed or contributed voluntarily may not be sacrificed on a private altar.

notes.he: ומנלן דנזיר דבר נידר ונידב דתנן [זה הכלל דבר הנידר ונידב קרב בבמת יחיד:
notes.en: And from where do we derive that a nazirite’s offering is something vowed and contributed? As we learned: This is the principle: Something vowed and contributed is sacrificed on a private altar.

messages.text: And we learned in another baraita:
The meal offerings and the offerings of a nazirite are sacrificed on a private altar; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: אלמא נידר ונידב חשיב ליה דאי לאו הכי לא הוה קרב בבמת יחיד:
notes.en: And the nazirite offerings are sacrificed on a private altar: Evidently it is considered vowed and contributed, for otherwise it would not be sacrificed on a private altar.

notes.dh: ותנן המנחות והנזירות בבמת יחיד דברי ר' מאיר
notes.he: הוה מצי לשנויי תנאי היא שהרי בפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיז.) פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי מאיר ומסיק התם דמנחות ונזירות איכא בינייהו:
notes.en: And we learned: The meal offerings and the nazirite offerings are sacrificed on a private altar; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir: [The Gemara] could have answered that it is a dispute of tanna’im, for in the last chapter of Zevaḥim (117a) the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Meir, and it concludes there that the difference between them is meal offerings and nazirite offerings.

messages.text: It is clear from these baraitot that the peace offering of a nazirite belongs in the category of offerings that are vowed or contributed voluntarily. If so, there is no need for it to be included separately by the verse.

Delete the phrase: Offering of a nazirite from here, i.e., from the baraita that considers it an offering that is vowed or contributed voluntarily. Only the nazirite vow itself is classified as voluntary; once the vow has been uttered, the ensuing offerings are obligatory.
messages.quote: The meal offerings and the offerings of a nazirite

notes.he: דאע"ג דנזירות באה עליו ע"י נדר אין הקרבנות נקראין נידר ונידב דהא לא נדר אלא מן היין והקרבן מאיליו מוטל עליו חובה:
notes.en: Delete the nazirite offerings from here: For even though naziriteship comes upon him through a vow, the offerings are not called vowed and contributed, since he vowed only [to abstain] from wine, and the offering is imposed on him as an obligation of itself.

notes.he: וה"ה דצריך כמו כן למיסמייה מההיא דפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיז: ע"ש) דאמר מנחות ונזירות איכא בינייהו:
notes.en: Delete the nazirite offerings from here: And by the same token one must likewise delete it from that [passage] in the last chapter of Zevaḥim (117b), which says: The difference between them is meal offerings and nazirite offerings.

notes.dh: ותניא המנחות והנזיר קרבין בבמת יחיד
notes.he: אלמא שלמי נזיר דבר נידר ונידב הוא מדקרב בבמת יחיד] אלא אמר רב יוסף סמי מן ההיא מתניתא דהמנחות והנזירות לא תיתניה דנזירות קרב בבמת יחיד [וליכא למימר דליהוי נידר ונידב] ורב דימי סבר תנאי היא (דהא מתני' דקתני דנזירות קריבה בבמת יחיד רבי מאיר ורבנן פליגי עליה ואמרי דלא קרבו בבמת יחיד) [הא רבי מאיר דקרבין בבמת יחיד והא רבנן דפליגי עליה בבמה דלא קרב דלא הוי נידר ונידב] ואנא דאמרי כרבנן:
notes.en: And it is taught: The meal offerings and the nazirite are sacrificed on a private altar. Evidently the nazirite’s peace offerings are something vowed and contributed, since they are sacrificed on a private altar. Rather, Rav Yosef said [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text attributes the deletion to Rav Yosef; the daf leaves it unattributed and the Davidson English gives it to Rav Dimi]: Delete from that baraita “the meal offerings and the nazirite offerings”; do not teach that the nazirite offerings are sacrificed on a private altar, and one cannot say that it is vowed and contributed. And Rav Dimi holds it is a dispute of tanna’im: this is Rabbi Meir, [who holds] they are sacrificed on a private altar, and that is the Rabbis, who disagree with him [and hold] it is not sacrificed on a private altar, since it is not vowed and contributed; and I say in accordance with the Rabbis.

messages.text: Is there one who said that the offering of a nazirite is not vowed or contributed voluntarily? But isn’t it written: “And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said to the king: Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the Lord, in Hebron. For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelled at Geshur in Aram, saying: If the Lord shall indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord” (II Samuel 15:7–8).

verse.he: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵלְכָה נָּא וַאֲשַׁלֵּם אֶת־נִדְרִי אֲשֶׁר־נָדַרְתִּי לַיהֹוָה בְּחֶבְרוֹן׃
verse.en: After a period of forty years had gone by, Absalom said to the king, “Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow that I made to GOD.

notes.he: משמע בחברון אלך ואשלמה שם נדרי וההוא נדר נזירות היה דאבשלום נזיר עולם היה ומשלשים לשלשים יום היה מגלח ומביא קרבן ומדהלך להקריב קרבנות נזירותיו בחברון דהיא במת יחיד שמע מינה נידר ונידב הוא:
notes.en: Which I have vowed to the Lord, in Hebron: This implies: In Hebron I will go and pay my vow there. And that vow was a vow of naziriteship, for Absalom was a permanent nazirite, and every thirty days he would shave and bring an offering. And since he went to sacrifice the offerings of his naziriteship in Hebron, which is a private altar, learn from it that it is vowed and contributed.

messages.text: What, is it not the case that Absalom asked his father for permission for him to go to Hebron to sacrifice an offering on a private altar?
No, Absalom did not go to Hebron to sacrifice his nazirite offerings. Rather, Absalom actually said that he undertook the principal vow to be a nazirite when he was in Hebron.

notes.he: האי בחברון וה"ק אלכה נא לבמה גדולה בגבעון דהתם הוא מזבח שעשה משה ואשלמה נדרי שנדרתי בחברון אבל לא שיביא הקרבן בחברון:
notes.en: It refers to his principal vow: This “in Hebron” [refers to the vow], and this is what he is saying: Let me go to the great altar in Gibeon, for there is the altar that Moses made, and pay my vow that I vowed in Hebron; but not that he would bring the offering in Hebron.

notes.he: למנות נזירות היינו עיקר נידרו:
notes.en: No, it refers to his principal vow, which he vowed in Hebron: to count naziriteship; that is his principal vow.

messages.text: Was his principal vow to be a nazirite in fact uttered in Hebron? But wasn’t the vow made when Absalom was in Geshur? After all, the verse states explicitly: “For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelled at Geshur.”
messages.quote: For your servant vowed a vow

notes.he: דכתיב כי נדר נדר עבדך בשבתי בגשור וגו':
notes.en: But wasn’t it in Geshur, etc.: As it is written: “For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelled at Geshur,” etc.

notes.he: והיה מגלח (מל' לל') [משנה לשנה] לחברון והוה תמן בתמיהא כלומר (דהתם נדר) [דסתם נדריה] מאן נפקא ליה מינה היכא נדר ואמאי אזיל להתם בשביל כך. ועוד הא בגשור הוה [נדרו:
notes.en: He was a permanent nazirite, and he would shave [from year to year] in Hebron, and he was there? This is said in astonishment: That is, [as for his vow in general,] what difference does it make where he vowed, and why would he go there on account of that? And furthermore, his vow was in Geshur.

messages.text: The verse means that Absalom went to Hebron only in order to bring sheep specifically from there.
messages.lead: Rav Aḥa said, and some say that it was Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan who said:

notes.he: ולהקריבן שוב בבמה גדולה וה"ק אשלמה את נדרי כלומר אשלמה את נזירותי ואגלח ומחברון אביא הכבשים ולהכי פריך מחברון מיבעי ליה:
notes.en: To bring sheep: And then to sacrifice them on the great altar. And this is what he is saying: I will pay my vow, that is, I will complete my naziriteship and shave, and from Hebron I will bring the sheep. And this is why he asks: It should have said “from Hebron.”

notes.he: בו כבשים שמנים במס' מנחות (דף פז.):
notes.en: In Hebron: there are fat sheep, [as stated] in tractate Menaḥot (87a).

notes.he: כדתניא אילים ממואב וכבשים מחברון דאי לא תימא הכי נזירות דחוצה לארץ היא דנדר בשבתו בגשור בארם ואין עולה לו מן המנין דהכי תנן במס' נזיר מי שנזר נזירות מרובה:
notes.en: That he went to take sheep from Hebron: As it is taught: Rams from Moab and sheep from Hebron. For if you do not say so, it was a naziriteship outside the Land, since he vowed while dwelling at Geshur in Aram, and it does not count toward his tally, for so we learned in tractate Nazir: “One who vowed a lengthy naziriteship…”

messages.text: This also stands to reason, as, if you say that Absalom went to Hebron to sacrifice his offering, would he have abandoned Jerusalem and gone to sacrifice in Hebron?

But rather, what is our explanation of the verse? That Absalom went to bring sheep from Hebron? If so, this verse that states: “Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the Lord, in Hebron” (II Samuel 15:7), should instead have stated: Which I have vowed to the Lord from Hebron.
Rather, actually Absalom did go to Hebron to sacrifice his peace offering as a nazirite.

notes.he: דנזירות בבמת יחיד:
notes.en: Rather, actually to sacrifice: For naziriteship [offerings may be sacrificed] on a private altar.

messages.text: And that which is difficult for you, i.e., why Absalom abandoned Jerusalem and sacrificed his offering in Hebron, should not pose a difficulty for you; rather, it is the question of why Absalom did not sacrifice his offering in Gibeon that should pose a difficulty for you, as at that time the Tabernacle and the communal altar were in Gibeon, and it was a sanctified place. Why, then, did Absalom go to Hebron rather than Gibeon?

notes.he: דשם מזבח שעשה משה:
notes.en: Gibeon should pose a difficulty for you: For there was the altar that Moses made.

messages.text: Rather, since the private altars were permitted, he was permitted to sacrifice wherever he wished, and he chose to go to Hebron. There was no reason for him to choose to go to Gibeon rather than any private altar.

notes.dh: אלא כיון דהותרו הבמות כל היכא דבעי מקריב
notes.he: ולרבנן דפליגי עליה דרבי מאיר דאמר נזיר לאו נידר ונידב הוא צריך לומר דלא הלך אבשלום אלא להביא כבשים מחברון ולהקריבן בגבעון מיהו לפי מה דפרש"י פרק בתרא דזבחים (ג"ז שם) דרבנן דרבי מאיר כרבנן בתראי סבירא להו דאמרי כאן וכאן לא קרבו ליחיד אלא עולה ושלמים בלבד קשה דא"כ היכי קאמר אבשלום אלכה נא ואשלמה את נדרי אשר נדרתי וגו' הא לאו נידר ונידב הוא נזירות לרבנן וא"כ כאן וכאן לא קרבי וצריך לחלק התנאים דרבנן דרבי מאיר לא ס"ל כרבנן בתראי אלא כרבי יהודה סבירא להו דאמר דבבמה גדולה אפי' חובות נמי קרבו ורבי מאיר דאית ליה נזירות דבר הנידר והנידב הא מצינו למימר דאית ליה כרבנן בתראי דזבחים דאמרי כאן וכאן לא קרבו ליחיד אלא עולה ושלמים בלבד מיהו ריהטא דשמעתא התם משמע כפרש"י מיהו תימה לר' שמעון דאמר התם בפ' בתרא דזבחים (גז"ש) אף ציבור לא הקריבו אלא פסחים וחובות הקבוע להם זמן ואמר בפ' כל שעה (פסחים לח:) זאת אומרת שחלות תודה ורקיקי נזיר נאכלין בנוב וגבעון ופרש"י שם דהיינו דלא כר"ש וא"כ היכי קאמר אבשלום אלכה נא ואשלמה את נדרי הרי לא היה יכול להקריבו ותירץ מורי הרמ"ר דרבי שמעון לטעמיה דאמר במסכת נזיר (דף מו:) דאם גילח על שלמי נדבה יצא ואם אמר הריני מגלח על מאה עולות יביא מאה עולות וא"כ אפשר דאבשלום נדר להביא עולות נדבה ודבר הנידר והנידב קרב בבמה לכ"ע ועליה היה אבשלו' רצה לגלח:
notes.en: In brief: Since private altars were permitted, he could sacrifice wherever he wished. (1) According to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Meir and hold that naziriteship is not vowed and contributed, one must say that Absalom went only to bring sheep from Hebron and sacrifice them in Gibeon. (2) But according to Rashi’s explanation in the last chapter of Zevaḥim, that Rabbi Meir’s disputants hold like the later Rabbis there, who say that at both the great and the small altars an individual sacrificed only burnt offerings and peace offerings, it is difficult: How could Absalom say “Let me go and pay my vow,” if for the Rabbis naziriteship is not vowed and contributed and could be sacrificed at neither? One must then divide the tanna’im: Rabbi Meir’s disputants do not hold like the later Rabbis but like Rabbi Yehuda, who says that at the great altar even obligatory offerings were sacrificed; while Rabbi Meir, who holds naziriteship is vowed and contributed, can hold like the later Rabbis of Zevaḥim. Yet the plain flow of the passage there implies as Rashi explained. (3) It is also difficult according to Rabbi Shimon, who says there (Zevaḥim) that even the community sacrificed [at Nov and Gibeon] only Paschal offerings and obligatory offerings with a fixed time; and it says in Pesaḥim (38b), “This is to say that the loaves of a thanks offering and the wafers of a nazirite were eaten in Nov and Gibeon,” which Rashi there explains is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. If so, how could Absalom say “Let me go and pay my vow,” since he could not sacrifice it? Their teacher, HaRaMaR, answered that Rabbi Shimon follows his own view in tractate Nazir (46b): if a nazirite shaved on voluntary peace offerings he has fulfilled his obligation, and if he said, “I will shave on one hundred burnt offerings,” he brings one hundred burnt offerings. So Absalom may have vowed voluntary burnt offerings, which everyone agrees are sacrificed at a private altar, and wished to shave on them. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Forty years, according to whose counting, i.e., forty years from when?
messages.quote: at the end of forty years

messages.text: The verse is referring to the end of forty years from when the Jewish people requested for themselves a king, in the days of Samuel (see I Samuel, chapter 8).
messages.lead: It is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Nehorai says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

messages.text: With regard to that year when they requested for themselves a king, that year was the tenth year of the leadership of Samuel.
Continued on 15a: the baraita counts the forty years, beginning with the ten years in which Samuel led alone.
